scope: local real child-process transport tests with synthetic bytes; no genesis decoding, compilation, ledger replay or network execution
change: Add optional bounded immutable stdin while draining stdout and stderr, deliver EOF by default, and retain existing owned-group cleanup and deadlines.

validation.skipReason: Existing Linux-only process-name truncation check on a non-Linux development host.
checks: Absent and explicitly empty input produce EOF without inherited terminal input.
Exactly 16 MiB of synthetic binary bytes arrive with the expected SHA256; the helper does not copy them into private stderr.
A child fills both output pipes before reading 1 MiB of input; all three streams complete without deadlock.
Oversized input, text and mutable/non-byte containers refuse before process creation.
An early-closed stdin produces a path-free failure and the owned child is reaped.
A child that never reads stdin hits the deadline and is killed/reaped; existing cancellation, descendant and output-bound tests still pass.

limitations: The helper writes bytes to a pipe; semantic consumption and report authenticity remain the pinned decoder and caller responsibility.
Executable fingerprint and file-selection checks remain caller requirements; this helper grants no host or tool admission.
The allocation-byte decoder and reserve input are not yet integrated into fresh genesis preparation.
Tests start only local synthetic Python children, not actual chain tools. No selected raw genesis or private key material is used.
